items.title: Antagonistic second-messenger signalling coordinates Pseudomonas aeruginosa surface colonization and virulence
items.abstract: Efficient colonisation of host tissue surfaces is a prerequisite for bacterial infection. In the human pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa , the second messengers cAMP and c-di-GMP regulate surface behaviours and virulence, but how these pathways are coordinated during tissue infection has remained unclear. Here we demonstrate that cAMP and c-di-GMP establish mutually exclusive signalling states at the single-cell level, generating distinct subpopulations of motile and surface-attached cells through pathway-specific control of type IV pili (T4P). Initial surface contact triggers an increase in c-di-GMP, activating FimW and driving stable attachment via bipolar T4P formation. This state is progressively replaced by cAMP, which inactivates FimW-dependent attachment and induces FimX-mediated T4P polarisation, surface motility and virulence activation. The resulting signalling transition enforces coexisting subpopulations, with attached cells gradually displaced by spreading cells. Using a human airway tissue model, we show that both T4P-mediated adhesion and twitching motility are required for invasion and tissue damage. Based on this, we propose that reciprocal cAMP–c-di-GMP signalling coordinates complementary T4P functions to optimise P. aeruginosa surface colonisation and infection.

items.title: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial
items.abstract: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. (Funded by Shenyang Science Tech Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657470) Medium-vessel occlusion accounts for a substantial proportion of acute ischemic stroke cases, yet optimal reperfusion treatment strategies remain unclear for patients ineligible for mechanical endovascular thrombectomy. Here, the authors show that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increases reperfusion rates for medium-vessel occlusion with acceptable safety, although statistically-significant improvements in 90-day functional outcomes were not detected in this phase-2 randomized trial.

items.title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase for acute basilar artery occlusion with sufficient recanalization after thrombectomy: the INSIST-IT randomized clinical trial
items.abstract: The clinical effect of adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase after successful recanalization in acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) remains uncertain. In this prospective, randomized, adaptive-enrichment, open label, blinded-end point, multi-center trial, patients with BAO within 24 h of estimated symptom onset who achieved successful reperfusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) were randomized (1:1) to intra-arterial tenecteplase (n = 75) or control (only received standard medical therapy, n = 69). The primary efficacy outcome was independent ambulation (modified Rankin Scale 0–3) at 90 days; the primary safety outcome was symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). The trial was stopped early due to safety concerns and lack of efficacy per Data Safety and Monitoring Committee recommendation. Among 144 randomized patients, 143 (99.3%) completed follow-up. At 90 days, independent ambulation was achieved in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 50.0% in the control group (OR 0.67; 95% CI 0.34–1.29; P = 0.23). sICH occurred in 6.2% versus 4.8% (OR 1.31; 95% CI 0.28–6.89; P = 0.73). All-cause mortality at 90 days was 41.3% versus 26.5% (OR 1.96; 95% CI 0.97–4.03; P = 0.063). In this prematurely terminated trial, adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase did not improve functional outcomes in patients with BAO. Acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) is a life-threatening cause of stroke, and whether intra-arterial tenecteplase after successful recanalization leads to improved outcomes is unclear. This randomized trial by Chen and colleagues was stopped early for safety concerns and shows that adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase does not improve functional outcomes in acute BAO.

items.title: Photoredox cobalt-catalyzed late-stage N-methyl-selective C–H vinylation of unactivated trialkylamines with alkynes
items.abstract: Late-stage functionalization of trialkylamine-containing drugs provides a direct way to access new chemical space, but selective modification of unactivated trialkylamines remains challenging because they contain multiple competing α-amino C–H bonds. Here we show a photoredox/cobalt dual-catalytic strategy for N-methyl-selective α-C–H vinylation of unactivated tertiary alkylamines with internal alkynes. This redox-neutral method provides trisubstituted allylic amines without directing groups or external oxidants, with broad substrate scope and high regioselectivity, stereoselectivity and site-selectivity under mild conditions. The reaction accommodates diverse amines and alkynes, including electronically unbiased dialkyl alkynes, and enables gram-scale synthesis, preparation of the fungicide fenpropidin and late-stage functionalization of structurally complex pharmaceuticals. Some drug analogues show enhanced apparent human histamine H1 receptor binding affinity. Mechanistic experiments and computational studies support a reasonable reaction pathway involving α-amino carbon radical generation via photoredox catalysis, followed by aminomethyl-cobalt I -mediated alkyne migratory insertion and protonolysis. This work provides a practical strategy for selective trialkylamines editing and late-stage diversification.

items.title: Phospholipase D1 activates NAD kinase fuelling neutrophil extracellular trap formation
items.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular trap formation is a central innate immune defence mechanism that depends on NADPH oxidase–driven reactive oxygen species production. How NADP⁺ availability is regulated during neutrophil activation remains unclear. Using integrated lipidomic, biochemical and functional analyses in human neutrophils, we identify NAD kinase, the sole enzyme responsible for NADP⁺ synthesis, as a direct lipid-regulated effector downstream of phospholipase D1. Neutrophil activation induces rapid, phospholipase D1-dependent production of phosphatidic acid and phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate, which bind and activate NAD kinase. The resulting cytosolic NADP⁺ is reduced to NADPH by the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway and consumed by NADPH oxidase during neutrophil extracellular trap formation. Pharmacological or genetic disruption of phospholipase D1 suppresses NAD kinase activity, depletes NADP⁺ and impairs neutrophil extracellular trap formation independently of direct NADPH oxidase inhibition. These findings define a lipid–metabolic axis coupling phospholipase D1-driven membrane remodelling to NADP⁺ availability and innate immune function.

items.title: [18F]FET PET enables histopathology-validated detection of non-contrast-enhancing glioblastoma
items.abstract: Accurate visualization of glioblastoma is essential for guiding biopsy, resection and radiotherapy. Contrast-enhanced MRI is routine in clinical practice, yet it can miss metabolically active tumor outside areas of blood-brain barrier disruption. In a histopathology-validated cohort with 472 tissue samples of 61 patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, we show that O-(2-[¹⁸F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET ([ 18 F]FET PET) depicts tumor tissue significantly better than contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI), especially in regions that show no enhancement on MRI. [ 18 F]FET PET achieves substantially higher sensitivity for tumor detection (91.2% vs 52.6%) and maintains high reliability in non-enhancing tissue (positive predictive value 98.3%), findings that are consistent across newly diagnosed and recurrent disease and in both cohorts undergoing either resection or biopsy. These results indicate that [ 18 F]FET PET complements MRI by revealing MRI-occult tumor burden. Incorporating amino acid PET into routine planning may therefore improve the accuracy of tumor visualization and, ultimately, patient management.

items.title: Diacylglycerol Metabolism Drives Host–pathogen Responses During Enteric Infection in Drosophila
items.abstract: Lipid metabolism is fundamental to cellular homeostasis, supporting energy storage, membrane architecture, and cellular signaling. Beyond these canonical roles, lipids have emerged as critical regulators of host immunity. Here, we define a lipid-driven mechanism that governs host–pathogen interactions by impacting pathogen clearance and thus infection outcomes. Exploiting Drosophila , we show that enteric infection triggers robust accumulation of neutral lipids, and specifically 1,2-diacylglycerols (DAGs), in the midgut. Disruption of DAG biosynthesis or lipid transport in midgut enterocytes (ECs) impairs lipid accumulation and reduces host survival. Conversely, dietary lipid supplementation enhances lipid storage and improves survival. Mechanistically, these lipid-dependent responses regulate defecation, thereby controlling bacterial clearance from the midgut. DAGs can act as signaling lipids that activate protein kinase C (PKC), and DAG accumulation in ECs correlates with elevated PKC activity and calcium signaling in midgut visceral muscle (VM), promoting VM contraction, midgut motility, and expulsion of pathogens via defecation. Together, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for DAG metabolism in shaping host defenses.

items.title: Effective enzyme engineering through modeling kinetic parameter changes upon mutations with geometric deep learning
items.abstract: Quantifying enzyme kinetic parameter changes upon mutations is essential for accelerating enzyme evolution. Current methods focus on predicting absolute values of kinetic parameters (turnover numbers kcat and Michaelis constants Km), yet they fail to accurately capture mutation effects. To our knowledge, no method directly models mutation effects (Δkcat and ΔKm) due to the scarcity of such training data. Moreover, these methods haven’t fully exploited protein structural geometry. Here, we establish a high-quality enzyme mutation effect dataset by pairing wild-type and mutant kinetic parameters measured under identical experimental conditions via a semi-automatic procedure combining language model-assisted parsing and manual verification. Leveraging this dataset, we develop DeltaCata, a Siamese geometric graph neural network to directly predict the changes in kinetic parameters induced by residue substitutions. DeltaCata demonstrates substantial performance improvements over existing methods, especially for enzymes unseen in the training sets. Its utility is further validated through in silico beneficial mutation screening experiments using deep mutational scanning datasets. Finally, we apply DeltaCata to engineer the methyltransferase sGmOMT2, achieving up to a 7.0-fold improvement in catalytic efficiency for in vitro icaritin synthesis. These results suggest the high potential of DeltaCata for industrial enzyme engineering. Predicting how mutations affect enzyme catalytic efficiency remains challenging. Here the authors build a benchmark dataset and develop DeltaCata, a geometric deep learning model that predicts changes in enzyme kinetics and guides enzyme engineering.

items.title: Personalized adjunctive phage therapy for difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections
items.abstract: Musculoskeletal infections (MSIs), including fracture-related infections (FRIs) and periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs), remain difficult to treat because of biofilm formation and increasing antimicrobial resistance. Bacteriophage therapy (PT) has re-emerged as a promising adjunctive strategy, although prospective clinical evidence remains scarce. Here, we prospectively evaluated adjunctive local PT in 13 patients with refractory MSIs treated within the multidisciplinary PHAGEFORCE framework at University Hospitals Leuven (BE). Following surgery, personalized phage preparations were administered through a closed drain system for 8–10 days alongside systemic antibiotics. Clinical, microbiological, immunological, and genomic data were collected. Four patients with refractory MSIs lacking suitable phages served as a control cohort. Clinical remission was observed in nine of eleven evaluable phage-treated patients (82%), whereas all control patients experienced infection recurrence during follow-up. PT was well tolerated, with no serious adverse reactions or clinically meaningful toxicity. Local phage titers remained detectable throughout therapy despite interpatient variability. Serum-mediated phage neutralization was observed during and after PT, and longitudinal genomic monitoring revealed patient-specific phage dynamics, neither of which was clearly associated with clinical outcome. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and safety of standardized local PT and support further evaluation of this approach in controlled clinical trials. In this prospective study, authors found that personalized adjunctive local phage therapy was feasible and well tolerated in difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections, with 9 of 11 evaluable patients achieving remission.

items.title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
items.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis , the causative agent of tuberculosis, remains the world’s deadliest pathogen 1 . Despite intensive study, many of its genes remain uncharacterized, which limits the insight that can be gained into tuberculosis biology and constrains drug development. Genetic interaction (GI) mapping is a powerful strategy to define functional relationships between genes by quantifying how the phenotypic effects of combined perturbations deviate from expectations based on single-gene perturbations 2,3 . Here we develop a dual-sgRNA CRISPR-interference platform that enables high-throughput GI mapping in mycobacteria. We address key technical challenges in library construction and data interpretation by incorporating unique barcodes for each sgRNA pair and implementing a robust statistical pipeline for GI detection. Focusing on essential genes, we generate comprehensive GI maps in the model mycobacterium Mycobacterium smegmatis and the pathogen M. tuberculosis . These maps recapitulate known biology, uncover thousands of previously unrecognized interactions and identify functional connections between essential genes and drug targets. By generating AlphaFold3-based protein–protein interaction predictions 4 for all gene pairs in our GI maps, we show that a subset of GIs is likely to reflect underlying physical associations. Validation of selected GIs confirms both novel biological relationships and opportunities for synergistic targeting. Overall, this work establishes a generalizable framework for dual-gene perturbation and defines the architecture of essential-gene networks in mycobacteria, advancing both our understanding of tuberculosis biology and the rational design of combination therapies.

Autoantibodies associate with clinical outcome in patients with melanoma treated with a dendritic cell-based vaccine
items.abstract: Increased B cell receptor signaling pathways in patients with melanoma correlates with a favorable clinical response to a cancer vaccine expressing multiple tumor-associated antigens. Here, we utilize phage immunoprecipitation sequencing (PhIP-seq) and Rapid Extracellular Antigen Profiling (REAP) assays to analyze the autoantibody profiles of patients with melanoma from a dendritic cell vaccine trial (NCT01622933), before and after vaccination. Patients have significantly elevated breadth and titer of autoantibodies compared to healthy donors. Vaccination results in the induction of de novo autoantibodies, particularly those with a favorable clinical outcome. Reduced serum SDF1-alpha, MIP-1ß, MCP1 and increased circulating monocytes are associated with development of autoantibodies. We identify plasma autoantibody signatures separating melanoma from healthy subjects as well as clinical responders vs non-responders to vaccination treatment. These findings demonstrate the potential for autoantibodies as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers that predict clinical outcomes in cancer. NCT01622933 was a clinical trial of an autologous dendritic cell-based vaccine in patients with melanoma. Here the authors show that the vaccine results in the induction of de novo autoantibodies associated with a favourable clinical outcome.

items.title: UNMASC: modelling non-monotonic dose responses to cytokine combinations
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) have been proposed as an alternative T cell source for CAR-T cell therapies, as they can be differentiated and matured into T cells in vitro using cytokines. These assays benefit from computational and mathematical models to design appropriate experimental protocols. However, models are limited by typical monotonic dose-responses, preventing them from being used for cytokine effects that are largely non-monotonic. To address this shortcoming, we developed Uncovering Non-Monotonic Antagonistic and Synergistic Combinations (UNMASC), a novel mathematical model describing non-monotonic dose-response surfaces of cytokine interactions that distinguishes synergy of efficacy and potency. We showed that our approach successfully recapitulates non-monotonic observed dose-response surfaces characterizing in vitro T cell progenitor differentiation. Our results highlighted cytokine combinations with antagonistic effects alone but synergistic in combination, particularly IL3 and IL7. Together, UNMASC accelerates the efficient cell generation assays and extends drug interaction surfaces to a broader range of dose-responses.

items.title: Alpha-aminoadipate in the saccharopine pathway promotes cancer metastasis through sumoylation of transcription machinery
items.abstract: Despite studies linking metabolism and cancer, our understanding of the metabolite network that drives metastasis remains incomplete. Through a metabolic RNAi-based screen for cell invasion, we identify alpha-aminoadipate (2-AAA), the intermediate metabolite of aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS) in the saccharopine pathway, as a common pivotal factor in metastasis of human cancers. Metabolite-protein connectivity mapping reveals that 2-AAA binds to SAE1, a crucial component of the SUMO-activating enzyme E1, and enhances SAE1 recruitment to UBA2, facilitating sumoylation. 2-AAA-mediated sumoylation of the RNA polymerase subunit POLR2A then partially promotes cancer cell invasion by inducing the expression of metastasis-promoting genes, including SPG11 and KCTD7 . Targeting AASS with cetalkonium chloride, a newly identified small molecule inhibitor against AASS, attenuates cancer cell invasion and tumor metastasis. Our study highlights the mechanism by which metastasis is mediated by metabolite-driven sumoylation and indicates AASS as an effective therapeutic target for mitigating metastatic cancer progression.

items.title: Wt1 splice isoforms bias lineage programmes during formative pluripotency
items.abstract: How transcriptional asymmetry arises in the epiblast before gastrulation remains a central question in mammalian development. Using a targeted CRISPRa screen, we identify Wt1 as a regulator of lineage-associated transcriptional programmes during formative pluripotency. Wt1 is transiently induced during formative pluripotency in vitro and in vivo, coincident with emerging lineage biases. Precocious Wt1 induction advances cells toward post-implantation identity, whereas Wt1 -deficient cells execute naïve exit but show impaired acquisition of formative and lineage-associated programmes. WT1 binds active regulatory elements together with OTX2, OCT4 and FOXO1. Comparison of Wt1 splice isoforms identifies KTS splice status as the major determinant of divergent anterior/neuroectodermal and posterior/mesodermal transcriptional programmes in vitro. In the E5.5 epiblast, Wt1 expression and splice composition align with lineage-biased states, linking isoform usage to anterior bias in vivo. Isoform-dependent programmes are conserved in human pluripotent cells. These findings identify alternative splicing as a mechanism tuning lineage-associated transcriptional bias before gastrulation.

items.title: A nanomolar-affinity antibody enabling sensitive labeling and high-resolution genomic mapping of O-GlcNAc
items.abstract: High-affinity O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc)-specific antibodies are crucial for the sensitive detection and functional study of O-GlcNAcylation. Here, we report the development of a nanomolar-affinity O-GlcNAc antibody named EPR19847 by using a degenerate O-GlcNAcylated peptide as the immunogen. The EPR19847 antibody can be used for O-GlcNAc detection, imaging, isolation, and chromatin immunoprecipitation. Using this antibody, O-GlcNAcylated proteins are enriched and identified in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). Chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by next-generation sequencing demonstrates that O-GlcNAc is enriched around the promoters of highly expressed genes, and that its genomic distribution is positively correlated with transcription-activating marks including H3K4me3, H3K9ac, and RNA polymerase II in mESCs. Further analysis suggests a high occupancy of O-GlcNAcylation within super-enhancers. We anticipate that EPR19847 will serve as a powerful tool for the highly sensitive detection and systematic functional dissection of O-GlcNAc. O‑GlcNAcylation is a widespread protein modification, but sensitive tools for its detection have been limited. Here, the authors develop a high‑affinity O‑GlcNAc antibody that enables detection, enrichment and genomic mapping of O‑GlcNAcylated proteins, revealing associations with active promoters and super‑enhancers.

items.title: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) prevents excessive protein aggregation and mediates aggrephagy by modulating the liquidity of p62 condensates
items.abstract: Loss of proteostasis can cause protein aggregation and trigger aggrephagy, yet how these biological processes are coordinated remains unclear. Here, we showed that p62 condensates transit from a gel-like to a more liquid-like state in response to proteotoxic stress. VHL was recruited to aggresomes and colocalizes with p62, which is crucial for p62 to perform its distinct functions in aggresome formation and autophagic degradation. Mechanistically, VHL binds to p62 through its IDR1 region and increases the liquid-like properties via IDR2 region. VHL depletion or disease-associated IDR2 mutations impair p62 condensate dynamics, leading to excessive accumulation of aggregated proteins and concomitant KEAP1 sequestration/NRF2 stabilization. A chimeric peptide linking the p62 PB1 domain to VHL IDR2 recapitulates VHL’s fluidity-promoting activity and suppresses tumorigenesis and protein aggregation. Overall, our findings reveal an HIF-independent tumor-suppressive role of VHL in regulating proteostasis and suggest a new treatment for cancer through the targeting of condensate dynamics. VHL shows an unexpected HIF-independent role in maintaining protein homeostasis under proteotoxic stress, namely, by increasing the liquidity of p62 condensates and orchestrating aggresome formation and subsequent aggrephagy.

items.title: Colonic enterochromaffin cells modulate a neuronal-immune-epithelial cell axis for antimicrobial homeostasis
items.abstract: The intestinal mucosa functions alongside trillions of commensal microbes, with immune and epithelial responses contributing to microbiota homeostasis. Both immune and nerve cells are implicated in this microbial balance, but the regulatory functions of epithelial enteroendocrine cells (EEC) are not understood well. Here we show that EEC depletion in mouse colons via Satb2-mediated Neurog3 deficiency enhances goblet cell expression of prominent antimicrobial peptides, with stronger effects in female than in male mice. Mechanistically, serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; 5-HT) derived from enterochromaffin (EC) cells, an EEC-subtype, acts on sensory neurons to suppress the mucosal levels of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) under physiological conditions. In the absence of local serotonin, elevated CGRP levels promote mast cell infiltration and interleukin-13 (IL-13) secretion in EEC-depleted mice and enhance antimicrobial gene expression in goblet cells. Our findings thus delineate an epithelial–neuronal–immune axis, wherein EC cells fine-tune goblet cell antimicrobial output to preserve gut microbial equilibrium. In the gut, epithelial, neuronal, and immune cells collaborate to maintain microbiota homeostasis, but molecular insights are still lacking. Here the authors deplete epithelial enteroendocrine cells in mouse colons via Satb2-mediated Neurog3 deficiency to uncover a serotonin/CGRP/IL-13 axis of antimicrobial peptide regulation that is validated in organoid cultures.

items.title: Triply convergent carbenylative Suzuki–Miyaura coupling enabled by palladium/copper co-catalysis
items.abstract: Pd-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura coupling is indispensable in modern organic synthesis, yet extending its modularity beyond two coupling partners remains challenging. Here we report a triply convergent cross-coupling that integrates aryl halides, aryl boronic acids, and N-tosylhydrazones through a Pd/Cu co-catalyzed process. By embedding a carbene insertion step into the Suzuki–Miyaura manifold and overcoming the longstanding chemoselectivity challenge between carbene insertion and direct cross-coupling, this strategy enables the construction of two C–C bonds at a central methine and grants access to three-dimensional chemical space with broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance. DFT studies indicate that the Cu co-catalyst governs the relative timing of transmetalation versus carbene insertion at two key junctures in the Pd catalytic cycle, thereby enforcing the desired reaction order. The utility of this method is demonstrated through streamlined syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds and analogues, alongside diverse downstream derivatizations. The palladium-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura coupling is indispensable in modern organic synthesis, yet extending its modularity beyond two coupling partners remains challenging. Here the authors report a triply convergent cross-coupling that integrates aryl halides, aryl boronic acids, and N-tosylhydrazones through a palladium/copper co-catalyzed process.

items.title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide and transcriptome-wide association analyses identify new risk loci and genes for inflammatory bowel disease
items.abstract: ABSTRACT To advance genetic understanding of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we conduct multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWAS) meta-analyses of 63,415 cases of Europeans and East Asians, and identified 60 previously unreported susceptibility loci. Integrating multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), cell type-specific TWAS, alternative splicing, and alternative polyadenylation analyses using RNA-sequencing data from normal colon tissues of 707 Europeans and 364 East Asians, we identify 441 candidate risk genes, including 324 not previously implicated by GWAS or TWAS, of which 291 were further supported by colocalization or summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analyses. These genes converge on pathways central to IBD pathogenesis (e.g., immune regulation), with over half showing transcriptional dysregulation supported by single-cell and spatial omics analyses. We further identify 44 druggable genes linked to 221 approved drugs or Phase II/III clinical-stage compounds. Our findings deepen the understanding of IBD genetics and provide insights for future research relevant to precision medicine for IBD.

items.title: PRMT6 suppresses intestinal inflammation by epigenetically repressing IL-1β in mouse models of colitis
items.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic inflammatory disorder driven by dysregulated immune responses. Macrophage-mediated inflammation is central to the pathology, and it is important to understand the epigenetic mechanisms involved. By screening epigenetic molecules that are differentially expressed in published human IBD datasets, we find Protein Arginine Methyltransferase 6 (PRMT6) consistently downregulated in IBD samples compared to healthy controls. Co-occurrence of Prmt6 suppression and Il1b induction within the myeloid compartment in colon biopsy samples indicates that PRMT6 limits macrophage-driven inflammation. Concordantly, Prmt6-deficient mice exhibit increased susceptibility to both DSS- and TNBS-induced colitis, characterized by exacerbated tissue damage and systemic elevation of IL-1β. Transcriptomic profiling confirms that PRMT6 deficiency selectively upregulates Il1b among inflammatory mediators. Mechanistically, PRMT6 suppresses Il1b transcription by interacting with RBBP5 and disrupting SET1A complex assembly, thereby reducing H3K4me3 enrichment at the Il1b promoter, independently of its canonical H3R2me2a catalytic activity. Furthermore, PRMT6 is transcriptionally silenced by the NF-κB subunit p50 during inflammation. Pharmacological inhibition of p50 restores PRMT6 expression, thus protecting mice from DSS-induced colitis in a PRMT6-dependent manner. Our findings highlight PRMT6 as a pivotal epigenetic regulator of the inflammatory response and provide proof of principle for targeting the p50–PRMT6–IL-1β axis in IBD. Epigenetic regulation in immune cells drive their physiological and pathologic development, including establishment of inflammatory states. Here the authors show in mouse colitis models, that genomic deletion of the protein arginine methyltransferase PRMT6 leads to a selective upregulation of IL-1β in macrophages and to exacerbated inflammation.

items.title: Honeybee (Apis mellifera) venom and its bioactive peptides tertiapin and apamin modulate the proteome of SARS-CoV-2-infected cells
items.abstract: The continuing emergence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) variants highlights the need for host-directed antiviral strategies with specific molecular mechanisms. Honeybee (Apis mellifera) venom (HBV) contains bioactive peptides with immunomodulatory and membrane-active properties, yet their effects on SARS-CoV-2 infection remain insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated the antiviral activity and proteomic impact of whole HBV and two venom-derived peptides, apamin (APA) and tertiapin (TERT), in human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2-expressing HEK293 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 spike-pseudotyped lentiviral particles. Cell viability and membrane integrity assays showed that HBV, APA, and TERT exerted limited cytotoxicity at the tested concentrations. In pseudovirus infectivity assays, HBV displayed the strongest inhibitory effect, reducing viral infectivity to 61.3% at 2 μg/mL, whereas APA reduced it to 73.3% at 0.5 μg/mL, and TERT showed weaker inhibitory activity. Comparative nano-liquid chromatography matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization tandem mass spectrometry revealed treatment-associated remodelling of the host-cell proteome. A shared signature of 215 proteins across HBV-, APA-, and TERT-treated infected cells was enriched in binding and catalytic activity, translational proteins, metabolite interconversion enzymes, cytoskeletal proteins, and pathways linked to integrin, Wnt, interferon, and Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription signalling. Protein-protein interaction analysis highlighted functional clusters associated with cytoplasmic translation, viral mRNA translation, and the Sec61 translocon complex, with EFTUD2, EPRS1, and HSPA4 emerging as central hubs. HBV treatment additionally promoted immune-related and interferon-stimulated gene products, including factors involved in innate antiviral defence, cytoskeletal organization, ion transport, and membrane structural reinforcement. These findings suggest that HBV reduces SARS-CoV-2 pseudovirus infectivity through a multifactorial host-directed mechanism involving antiviral signalling, cellular architecture, and proteostasis, supporting further investigation of bee venom-derived compounds as antiviral agents.

items.title: Water-Mediated Organocatalytic Formal [6 + 1] Cycloaddition via Redox-Neutral Triple sp3 C–H Alkylation: Green Access to Azepinoindole-Linked Indolenines
items.abstract: A water-mediated organocatalytic formal [6 + 1] cycloaddition of 2-methyl indolenines with dielectrophilic 4-amino-indole-3-carbaldehydes has been achieved through redox-neutral triple sp3 C–H alkylation. A series of azepinoindole-linked indolenines were synthesized in good yields with excellent diastereoselectivities (up to 94% yield, >20:1 dr). This method has notable features such as water as the green reaction medium, metal-free and redox-neutral conditions, atom economy, broad substrate scope, late-stage modification of drug molecules, and gram-scale synthesis.

items.title: Transformer‐Guided Co‐Optimization of Mutation Prioritization and Thermodynamic Probe Design for Mutation Detection
items.abstract: The design of sequence‐selective DNA probes has long been limited by a decoupled workflow in which target selection proceeds without considering the physicochemical determinants of probe performance, such as thermodynamic stability and mismatch discrimination. Here, we establish an iterative computational design strategy that unifies mutation prioritization with chemical probe design. A custom transformer model extracts diagnostic attribution scores of mutations from 1,782 samples, generating semantic maps to guide probe placement. Candidate designs undergo in silico thermodynamic screening based on differential binding free energy. Probes failing to satisfy the integrated criteria of thermodynamic discrimination, diagnostic attribution, and population frequency are further evaluated by refining their spatial configuration to co‐optimize thermodynamic discriminability and clinical relevance. This iterative process converges on an 8‐plex targeted panel. Wet laboratory validation confirms 0.03% variant allele frequency detection with low assay cost and short turnaround time. Clinical testing on 375 samples achieves AUROC values of 0.96 for tissue and 0.90 for plasma. This work provides a potential chemical framework for nucleic acid probe design that could be explored in other molecular diagnostic systems.

items.title: This cholesterol drug promised to be a game-changer. Why did it flop in the clinic — and is there still hope?
Relaxase asymmetry drives initiation of bacterial conjugation
items.abstract: Bacterial conjugation drives horizontal gene transfer and accelerates the spread of antibiotic resistance. In F-plasmid systems, the bifunctional relaxase-helicase TraI initiates transfer by nicking plasmid DNA through its trans-esterase activity and subsequently unwinding the plasmid via its helicase domains. Previous evidence suggested that two TraI molecules act cooperatively, yet how their activities are spatially and temporally coordinated has remained unclear. Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of a functionally asymmetric TraI homodimer and show that dimerisation is mediated predominantly by single-stranded DNA. Trans-esterasedriven duplex melting at the origin of transfer by one TraI molecule enables helicase loading by a second TraI molecule onto the transfer strand of the intact plasmid. Although the trans-esterase domain is intrinsically active, the host factor IHF inhibits nicking until helicase loading occurs. These findings uncover a regulatory loop coupling strand nicking with helicase engagement, defining a unified mechanism for initiating conjugative DNA processing.

items.title: Vasomechanic treatment is associated with increased efflux of human brain proteins
items.abstract: An age-related neurovascular impairment in nitric oxide (NO)-mediated vasodilation and reciprocal Piezo1-dependent vascular vasoconstriction may precede the accumulation of soluble brain proteins such as amyloid-β (Aβ) and disruption of brain fluid homeostasis in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Preclinical studies suggest that restoring these pathways can enhance neurofluid transport and improve cognitive outcomes. In this study (EudraCT 2021-000625-27), we investigated the effects of sublingual NO and Piezo1-targeted whole-body vibrations (WBV p ) in healthy adults ( n = 29) using multimodal neuroimaging and blood biomarker analysis. The combined intervention (NO+WBV p ) was associated with correlating changes in brain fluid dynamics and increased blood levels of soluble brain-derived proteins (Aβ 40&42 , GFAP). These effects increased with age and the magnitude of NO-induced hypotension. The interventions were well tolerated under controlled experimental conditions. Overall, the findings are consistent with transient redistribution of brain-derived proteins toward circulation, suggesting a potential non-invasive approach to increase neurofluidic solute efflux in humans. Pre-specified primary endpoints, changes in circulating brain-derived protein concentrations, brain fluid imaging and brain pulsation measures, were met. Secondary outcomes included physiological analyses.

items.title: Hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis prevents pro-metastatic niche formation through metabolic rewiring of inflammatory monocytes
items.abstract: Inositol-requiring enzyme 1α (IRE1α) and the downstream spliced form of X-Box Binding Protein 1 (XBP1s) have been identified as tumor promotors. However, how IRE1α–XBP1s signaling affects tumor progression in a non-cell autonomous manner remains unclear. Here we show that the hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis unexpectedly inhibits liver metastasis by confining local metainflammation. Genetic ablation of IRE1α or XBP1 in mouse hepatocytes exacerbates liver metastasis due to the accumulation of inflammatory monocytes (IMs). Mechanistically, a non-canonical Forkhead box O1 (FoxO1)-glutamine synthetase (GS) pathway endows the IRE1α- or XBP1-null hepatocytes with the metabolic activity to secrete glutamine, which is necessary and sufficient for IM fitness. Reintroduction of hepatocyte XBP1s or blockade of glutamine metabolism effectively reduces IMs and mitigates disease progression. Importantly, clinical patient survival with liver metastases positively correlates with hepatocyte XBP1s expression. Our study defines a paradigm of hepatocyte–IM interaction that can be leveraged to treat liver metastasis.

items.title: Overconsumption of low-digestible sugars can increase susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium infection
items.abstract: Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. However, we show that acute overconsumption of certain LDCs, particularly low-digestible sugars (LDSs), such as arabinose, lactulose, and polyols commonly used as sugar substitutes, can compromise colonization resistance against the common foodborne pathogen Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. LDS overconsumption results in elevated fecal pathogen loads, systemic dissemination, and colitis in infected mice. Mechanistic analysis of arabinose overconsumption revealed that rapid fermentation acidifies the intestinal environment, perturbs the microbiota, alters gut-luminal short-chain fatty acid levels and elevated amino acid availability, which can support pathogen growth. Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella . Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence.

items.title: Combing-triggered electrostimulation synchronizing deep delivery for rapid hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia
items.abstract: Androgenetic alopecia affects over 1.5 billion individuals, causing progressive hair loss with psychological and quality-of-life burdens. Current pharmacological treatment for androgenetic alopecia faces challenges due to systemic side effects from oral medications or limited efficacy of topical applications. Herein we develop a comb-shaped bioelectronic system, named “Detangle”, for efficient androgenetic alopecia treatment during daily hair combing. This system features electronic teeth embedded with height-differentiated electrodes and integrated drug-loading modules, which generate an enhanced electric field penetrating up to ~9 times deeper into hair follicle regions than conventional external application. We show that the localized electric field synchronizes electro-stimulating hair follicles, and electro-delivering vascular endothelial growth factor A encoding plasmid and steroid 5-alpha-reductase 2 targeting siRNA into follicular cells to promote angiogenesis and suppress androgen synthesis. Through the synergistic regulation of cellular metabolism, the system significantly increases hair restoration efficacy in an androgenetic alopecia mouse model, improving the outcome from ~70% to nearly 100% within one month compared to conventional topical minoxidil treatment. The Detangle system proves safe and effective for deep tissue delivery in dermatology. Here authors introduce a comb‑shaped bioelectronic device that uses enhanced electric fields for electrostimulation and deep acid delivery for androgenetic alopecia treatment. In mouse models, they show that this safe, non‑invasive approach achieves nearly 100% hair regrowth within one month.

items.title: Spatial protein interactomics in solid primary human tissue
items.abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) in diseased tissues represent a promising class of potential drug targets. However, PPIs are typically identified in live cells, lysate, and genetically engineered model organisms, limiting their translational value to human disease. Here we describe MAP-IT, an optimized photocatalytic carbene-based proximity labeling method for direct PPI mapping in primary human tissue sections, which bypasses the need for model organisms in the initial discovery step. We use MAP-IT to profile PPIs in situ for cell surface and nuclear target proteins, identify and orthogonally validate new interactors of EGFR in colon cancer, and couple light-powered MAP-IT labeling with spatially patterned visible light irradiation guided by neural network image segmentation to map location-specific protein interactomes. Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) represent a promising class of drug targets. Here, the authors describe MAP-IT, a photocatalytic carbene-based proximity labeling method for direct PPI mapping in primary human tissue sections.

items.title: Systematic Evaluation of Halogen Substitution in ortho-Benzoxy Phenylboronic Acid Catalysts for Amidation Reactions
items.abstract: Boronic acids have emerged as powerful catalysts for amidation reactions. Based on a previously identified orthobenzoxy phenylboronic acid motif, a systematic structure-activity study was performed. A catalyst library spanning F, Cl, Br, and I substitution on the ortho-benzoxy substituent was synthesized and evaluated as catalysts in amidation reactions. Catalytic activity increased in the order F < Cl < Br < I and followed the substitution pattern ortho < para < meta, with the meta-iodo derivative showing the highest conversion. This systematic comparison established structure-activity relationships within the catalyst library and provides a basis for the design of more efficient amidation catalysts

items.title: Enantio-Complementary Synthesis of Atropisomeric C–N Biaryl Amines via Imine Reductase-Mediated Dynamic Kinetic Resolution
items.abstract: C–N axially chiral biaryl amines constitute privileged scaffolds in drug discovery and asymmetric catalysis, yet they remain synthetically challenging due to low rotational barriers and inherent conformational flexibility. While biocatalysis presents an attractive avenue for constructing chiral amines, the lack of mirror-image enzymes has historically limited access to all stereoisomers. Here, we develop an unconventional biocatalytic platform leveraging dynamic kinetic reductive amination to synthesize C–N axially chiral biaryl amines in both enantiomeric forms. Through systematic screening and enzyme engineering, we achieved the synthesis of diverse aryl indole atropisomers with exceptional yields and enantioselectivities (up to 99% yield and 99% ee). Strikingly, we uncovered a unique stereo-divergent behavior wherein a single biocatalyst switches its stereochemical outcome solely by toggling the amine partner between alkylamines and arylamines. Mechanistic investigations using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations unveiled the origins of the high enantioselectivity, the substrate-dependent stereochemical reversal, and the catalytic enhancement imparted by a single point mutation. This study not only provides a robust platform for accessing elusive C–N axial chirality but also exemplifies the synergy between enzyme engineering and computational modeling in achieving stereo-divergent synthesis.

items.title: Novel triazolo[1,5]benzodiazepines as potent dual AChE/BChE inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease: synthesis, characterization, in vitro and in silico studies
items.abstract: Targeting Alzheimer's disease, a cycloaddition route furnishes triazolo[1,5]benzodiazepines with potent, picomolar dual AChE/BChE inhibition, validated by X-ray, NMR, HRMS, and molecular docking.

items.title: Decision stability of a default docking pipeline: a seed, box-placement, and protomer audit on LIT-PCBA MTORC1
items.abstract: Agentic and automated drug-discovery workflows increasingly call molecular docking as a black-box subroutine and act on its ranked output, typically from a single run under software defaults. We ask a narrow, operational question: if the same default pipeline is re-run with a different random seed, a slightly displaced search box, or a different input protomer, which decisions-the top-k compounds a downstream agent would advanceactually change? Using AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on the LIT-PCBA MTORC1 target (PDB 4jsx) with a fixed, score-blind panel of 60 ligands (20 actives, 40 inactives), we predeclared the decision rule and the seed and box-placement perturbation axes against a baseline, added a protomer arm whose selection criterion was amended during execution (disclosed with dates), and compared top-12 decision sets as symmetric differences (exits and entries), Jaccard indices, and binary decision changes, with pose quality checked by PoseBusters against the exact receptor used for docking. A positive control (redocking the co-crystallized ligand, symmetry-corrected RMSD 0.647 Å) validated the setup. Changing only the random seed replaced 3 of 12 top-12 members (6/60 binary decisions changed); a 2 Å box shift along x replaced 2, along y replaced 4; protomer changes at pH 7.0 replaced none. Eight ligands accounted for all flips, and the single PoseBustersinvalid pose was also a recurrent flipper. A threeseed majority-vote consensus cost 3× compute, dropped the invalid recurrent flipper, and still disagreed with every individual run; we report it as a priced mitigation with measured residual disagreement, not as certified stabilization. All results concern decision repeatability only: nothing here establishes that any decision set is correct, and a consensus can stabilize a wrong answer. All code, inputs, checkpoints, and negative results are provided in an accompanying archive prepared for the author; no public release has been made.

items.title: Randomized PEG-Based Polycarbonate Micelles with PEG-like Stealth Properties and Biodistribution
items.abstract: The increase in anti-PEG antibodies (APAs) as well as PEG-related adverse effects have questioned the benefits of PEGylated nanotherapeutics. Growing awareness of the safety and efficacy of PEGylation has prompted research into countermeasures, including alternative polymers. Among these, randomized PEG (rPEG) was established as a fundamentally new approach that preserves the polyether structure while preventing antibody recognition through isomerization. Here, rPEG was incorporated into polymeric micelles (PMs) for immunodrug delivery to assess its suitability as a PEG replacement. Amphiphilic rPEG polycarbonate block copolymers were synthesized via chain extension using rPEG macroinitiators with primary hydroxy end groups. The respective PMs self-assembled via solvent-exchange evaporation, encapsulating the hydrophobic TLR7/8 agonist CL075 as the immunodrug. rPEG-based PMs demonstrated size distributions and encapsulation efficiencies similar to those of PEG. In vitro assays confirmed that rPEG-PMs had comparable cellular uptake, no cellular toxicity, and similar drug-delivery efficiencies to PEG-PMs. Notably, competitive ELISAs revealed markedly decreased antigenicity of rPEG-PMs towards backbone- and end group-specific APAs. In a fiveday biodistribution study, rPEG-PMs showed whole-body and organ distribution patterns comparable to mPEG-PMs, as would be expected for a stealth polymer. Strikingly, despite the immunostimulatory payload, serum ELISA after a single dose detected anti-rPEG IgM in one of five mice, compared with anti-PEG IgM in three of five mice receiving mPEG-PMs, suggesting lower immunogenic potential for rPEG-PMs, though this remains to be confirmed in repeat-dose studies. Overall, these results position rPEG as a highly promising alternative to PEG for polycarbonate-based PMs and next-generation nanotherapeutics.

items.title: A Zwitterionic Indylene with Ambiphilic Redox Reactivity
items.abstract: Extending transition-metal-like organometallic redox chemistry to indium remains a challenge in molecular main-group chemistry. Here, we report a zwitterionic indylene supported by an anionic bis(N-heterocyclic carbene)borate ligand that displays diverse redox reactivity. Computational and structural analyses reveal a relatively narrow HOMO–LUMO gap together with a stabilizing arene–In interaction involving a vacant indium p orbital, endowing the In(I) centre with complementary donor and acceptor character. This ambiphilicity is expressed experimentally through coordination and reactivity, with a broad range of bond-forming and redox processes, including cycloaddition and the direct oxidative addition of unactivated aryl–halogen bonds. These results expand the accessible reactivity of molecular In(I) and establish bis(NHC)borate ligands as a powerful platform for the development of indium redox organometallic chemistry.

items.title: Exploiting Carboxylate Effects to Enhance Cp*Co III -Catalyzed C–H Functionalization
items.abstract: Carboxylates are ubiquitous additives in Cp*Co III -catalyzed C–H functionalization, yet their influence on catalyst speciation and catalytic performance remains poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that carboxylate choice can markedly improve reaction efficiency, particularly for substrates bearing weakly coordinating directing groups. Combining high-throughput experimentation (HTE) and reaction optimization, we identified mesitoic acid (MesCO 2 H) as an effective additive for hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE), outperforming conventional carboxylates. We then examined the influence of mesitoate and acetate on Cp*Co III speciation, isolating the corresponding dinuclear complexes. Catalytic studies in HIE revealed that both dimers are catalytically competent, but their activity depends on carboxylate identity and substrate coordination ability, with the mesitoate derivative exhibiting higher activity toward weakly coordinating substrates. We also report the first crystal structure of a direct analogue of the mononuclear κ 2 -carboxylate Cp*Co III species proposed as a putative intermediate prior to C–H activation. The isolated mesitoate-bridged dimer enabled C–H deuteration of pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals and proved effective beyond HIE in three distinct C–H functionalizations. Together, these findings highlight that carboxylate selection can play a decisive role in fine-tuning Cp*Co III catalysis, offering new opportunities for rational reaction optimization. KEYWORDS: Cp*Co III catalysis; C–H activation; catalyst speciation; carboxylates

items.title: ETALON: Verified Execution and Persistent Research Memory for Agentic Computer-Aided Drug Design
items.abstract: Language-model agents can coordinate computational drug discovery, but adapting a campaign to new evidence requires scientific software that supports flexible workflows, consistent modeling, and continuity across research sessions. Here we present ETALON, a harness that equips a general-purpose coding agent with an integrated environment for computer-aided drug design. Three independently usable systems supply its scientific operations: MolQuarry for chemical and biological evidence, MolCascade for molecular preparation, screening, and docking, and PRISM for molecular generation and physical modeling. Each exposes configurable procedures with explicit scientific requirements, so the host can revise its research strategy while retaining consistent preparation and evaluation practices. Operations registered with a common execution layer are checked before dispatch, and their outputs carry separate records of completion, verification, and admission, so that an incomplete computation is not recorded as an unfavorable molecular result. A persistent research graph links evidence, judgments, experiments, and results across sessions, and candidate method revisions are compared with frozen baselines under criteria declared in advance.

items.title: From Photo-crosslinking to Covalent: A Cascade DNA-Encoded Library Strategy for Pin1 Inhibitor Discovery
items.abstract: Peptidyl-prolyl cis–trans isomerase NIMA-interacting 1 (Pin1) plays vital biological roles in vivo and has been studied as a therapeutic target for a variety of human diseases. Covalent inhibitors represent the mainstream strategy in current Pin1 drug discovery, however, existing covalent molecules still rely on known affinity scaffolds or direct screening. Herein, we developed an innovative cascade DNA-encoded library (DEL) strategy that integrates photo-crosslinking with covalent targeting, enabling the de novo design of novel Pin1 covalent inhibitors. Photo-crosslinking DEL (PDEL) selection was first used to identify low-affinity binding fragments. These fragments then served as the beginning for covalent focused DELs (Co-FDEL) construction. Finally, covalent DEL selection led to the identification of two hits, LWH-1 and LWH-2, which covalently modify Pin1 at Cys113, with IC50 values of 447.4 nM and 273.7 nM. This strategy facilitates the rational evolution of low-affinity fragments to potent covalent inhibitors, offering an accelerated pathway for targeting challenging proteins.

items.title: Functional characterization of a hyperthermophilic glycyl radical enzyme reveals a reductive glycerol pathway in archaea
items.abstract: The function of the glycyl radical enzyme (GRE) PFL2 from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Archaeoglobus fulgidus has remained unresolved since its discovery. Structural and sequence analyses initially suggested that PFL2 was a B12-independent glycerol dehydratase (GDHt), whereas subsequent structural and transcriptional evidence implicated it as a methylalkylsuccinate synthase involved in anaerobic alkane activation. Difficulties in reconstituting active PFL2 in vitro prevented either assignment from being established biochemically. Here, genome mining identified soluble activating enzymes that enabled us to demonstrate that PFL2 catalyzes glycerol dehydration to 3-hydroxypropionaldehyde (3-HPA). This reaction initiates the reductive glycerol pathway, in which 3-HPA is subsequently reduced to 1,3-propanediol (1,3-PD), an industrially important precursor to polymers and other materials. Although characterized in bacteria, this pathway has not previously been experimentally established in archaea. Motivated by this knowledge gap, we identified three oxidoreductases encoded in the A. fulgidus genome that catalyze the reduction of 3-HPA to 1,3-PD in vitro. Microscale thermophoresis revealed nanomolar-affinity binding between PFL2 and one of these oxidoreductases, AF0339 (apparent Kd = 70–90 nM), and AlphaFold-Multimer modeling predicted a continuous tunnel connecting their active sites, suggesting a possible route for intermediate transfer. Notably, PFL2 and AF0339 exhibited melting temperatures of 80.5 and 85.2 °C, respectively, revealing a thermally stable pair of enzymes catalyzing both steps of the pathway. Together, these findings establish PFL2 as an archaeal GDHt and provide experimental support for a reductive glycerol pathway in archaea. The thermostability of these enzymes further highlights their potential utility in biocatalytic 1,3-PD production.

items.title: Yield Prediction and Condition Recommendation on High-Throughput Experimentation Datasets: Encoding Effects and Noise Ceilings
items.abstract: High-throughput experimentation (HTE) supplies enough reaction data to train machine-learning models, yet yield-prediction models are typically reported on a single dataset, and both their cross-dataset stability and their attainable ceiling are rarely examined. Using a single pipeline without per-dataset tuning, this work compares five model architectures under three categorical encodings on thirteen HTE datasets drawn from five public source collections, and estimates a noise ceiling for every dataset that repeats a condition. Accuracy is governed by the encoding rather than by the algorithm: switching a multilayer perceptron from integer to one-hot encoding raises its mean held-out R2 by 0.168. Across datasets, the spread in validation-selected held-out R2 tracks the noise ceiling, with a mean capture ratio of 86.35%. Attribution rankings show some regularity: the reactant slots rank at the top, followed by temperature and the additive, while the equivalence and metal slots carry the smallest mean shares. The limits are equally clear: substrate-disjoint and ordered cross-validation both give negative R2, and no cross-dataset transfer succeeds, so the framework supports interpolation only. On the only dataset with enough distinct reactant pairs, predicting unseen combinations of known reactants reaches R2 = 0.58, whereas predicting unseen reactants with molecular fingerprints reaches 0.41. Ranking by predicted yield outperforms expected improvement, whose uncertainty signal neither ranks the error nor is calibrated.

items.title: Umpolung of a Diazo Sulfonyl Fluoride Surrogate Expands Diversity-Oriented Clicking to Cyclopropanes
items.abstract: Herein, we report the synthesis of a new hypervalent iodine reagent, ((((( tert butyldimethylsilyl)oxy)methyl)sulfonyl)(diazo)methyl)(phenyl)- λ 3-iodaneyl trifluoromethanesulfonate (HIR 3 ), from the Diversity-Oriented Clicking (DOC) hub tert -butyl(((diazomethyl)sulfonyl)methoxy)dimethylsilane ( t Bu-DMSM), thereby reversing the native reactivity of its diazo carbon. Reaction of 3 with nucleophilic silyl enol ethers affords β-diazosulfones in good to excellent yields. Subsequent rhodium-catalysed intramolecular 1,3-C–H insertion provides novel cyclopropanes bearing a masked sulfonyl fluoride group in good to excellent yields and diastereoselectivities. Unmasking of this group enables the late-stage formation of cyclopropyl sulfonyl fluorides, either from the isolated cyclopropanes or through a one-pot, two-step sequence from the βdiazosulfones. We further demonstrate that the major cyclopropane diastereomer undergoes base-mediated epimerisation to afford an otherwise inaccessible diastereomer, which participates in sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) reactions to furnish the corresponding sulfonates. Finally, trapping of the intermediate sulfinate with benzyl bromide electrophiles, rather than conversion into the sulfonyl fluoride, provides access to structurally diverse sulfones.

items.title: Substrate Promiscuity of the Aryl-ACP Ligase AltC from the Alterochromide
items.abstract: Alterochromides are antibacterial and cytotoxic lipopeptides produced by Pseudoalteromonas , whose biosynthesis is proposed to begin with the loading of p -coumaric acid ( 1 ) onto the acyl carrier protein (ACP) AltB by AltC, an enzyme annotated as an AMP-binding protein. Herein, we report the characterization of AltC as an aryl-ACP ligase by heterologous expression and in vitro reconstitution with AltB, monitored by UPLC-MS. AltC catalyzes the loading of p -coumaric acid ( 1 ) onto holo-AltB and also accepts its brominated analog, 3-bromo-4-hydroxycinnamic acid ( 4 ), as well as 14 additional cinnamic acid analogs functionalized with hydroxyl, halogen, alkyl, alkoxy, amino and cyano substituents. For electron-poor substrates, the loaded ACP undergoes DTT addition, the extent of which decreases as the ring becomes more electron-rich. Given the broad substrate tolerance, AltC is unlikely to be the selectivity filter for the aryl acid incorporated into (bromo)alterochromides. The promiscuity of AltC also makes it a candidate biocatalyst for preparing non-natural aryl-ACPs and (bromo)alterochromide analogs.

items.title: Chiral Separation of Hexahydrocannabinolic Acid (HHCA) Isomers Have Differential Activity Against Jurkat T Cells
items.abstract: The use of phytocannabinoid compounds has exploded since the opening up of medicinal and recreational cannabis markets as well as the legalization of industrial hemp. Chemical derivatives of the naturally occurring phytocannabinoids have been explored as novel therapeutics to treat numerous diseases and medical conditions. Here, we describe a new chemically modified phytocannabinoid derivative, namely hexahydrocannabinolic acid (HHCA), produced from plant-derived tetrahydrocannabinolic acid (THCA). Catalytic hydrogenation of THCA affords HHCA as a diastereomeric mixture at the 9-position on the ring that was separated chromatographically into the isolated 9R and 9S isomers. We assessed their cytotoxic activity on Jurkat T cells and, while a mixture of both isomers of HHCA were found to be more active than THCA, the isolated 9S HHCA isomer was significantly more active than the 9R HHCA isomer. This finding offers not only new molecules to assess for drug discovery, but possibly new mechanisms of action for chemically modified phytocannabinoids.
